content:
Four identities carry this whole chapter. Students who see 103 × 97 and think "(100 + 3)(100 − 3) = 9991" bank the mark in ten seconds. Students who multiply long-hand spend ninety — and often slip. Start by testing the ground. The free IMO Class 8 Algebraic Expressions online test below asks 10 exam-pattern MCQs and scores them on the spot. Each explanation shows the intended one-minute route.

What the IMO asks from Algebraic Expressions in Class 8

  • Adding, subtracting and multiplying polynomials.
  • The identities: (a + b)², (a − b)², a² − b², (x + a)(x + b).
  • Mental products like 103 × 97 and 998 × 1002.
  • Evaluating a² + 1/a² from a + 1/a.
  • Simplifying and comparing expression values.

Key facts and formulas to revise first

  • (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b² — so 998 × 1002 = 10⁶ − 4 = 999996.
  • (x + a)(x + b) = x² + (a + b)x + ab — the middle term is a SUM, the last a PRODUCT.
  • If a + 1/a = 5, then a² + 1/a² = 5² − 2 = 23.
  • (a + b)² − (a − b)² = 4ab — a one-line bridge between sums and products.

Mistakes that cost Olympiad marks

  • Expanding (a + b)² as a² + b² — the 2ab term is the whole point.
  • Getting the middle sign wrong in (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b².
  • Multiplying x² × x³ as x⁶ instead of x⁵.

questions.q: If (2x + 3)(x - 4) - (x + 6)(2x - 5) = ax + b, find a² + b².
For what value of k does (x + 2) divide x³ + kx² - 4x + 12 exactly?
questions.explanation: By the factor theorem, f(-2) = 0. f(-2) = -8 + 4k + 8 + 12 = 4k + 12 = 0, so k = -3. Verify: x³ - 3x² - 4x + 12 = (x + 2)(x - 2)(x - 3).
This expression has the form a² + b² + 2ab = (a + b)². So (0.87 + 0.13)² = 1² = 1.
